transcript.text: One of my favorite price negotiation
techniques. How can you get a vendor to
lower their price for real? I will ask a
question that every vendor wants to
hear, which is how much is the maximum
amount that you can create of the thing.
They'll then give me either no response
or they'll give me a massive number. If
they give me a massive number, I say
great. Assume I can take up 100% of your
capacity, what would my volume discount
be at that price point? They'll
typically get excited at that point and
tell me what the price would be at that
volume. Once I know that price, I know
much closer to what their true bottom
is. And so then I can have way more
power saying, "Hey, I'm going to build
up to that, but I want to start with
this up front with the intention of
building to that volume." And so it's a
great way to kind of ethically find out
where the lines are for negotiation.
Now, if the person doesn't give you an
amount, then I'll typically say, "Okay,
well, if I were to" and then I basically
net out my goal for whatever the thing
that I'm selling is, how much volume I'd
love to sell in 5 years. I ask that so I
can reverse it into my model and I make
that clear. I want to be able to model
this out 5 years from now when we hit
the volume that I'm looking for. What
can I model from you?" They tell me that
answer and both of them accomplish the
same objective.
